Biomass Porous Carbon Derived from Celery Leaves with
High Capacitance for Supercapacitor
Jiaqi Wu, Zihan Ma, Guangning Wang,* and Tingting Chen*
[a]
To develop environmentally friendly and high-performance
supercapacitors, the low-cost, high-capacitance renewable
electrode material is at present viewed as one of the most
challenging tasks for obtaining the next-generation of energy
storage devices. Therefore, in this study, Celery leaves, a
common biomass vegetable, are used to prepare activated
carbon for high voltage and high-capacity supercapacitors
through a simple method. Due to their high surface area and
abundant nitrogen and sulfur heteroatoms, hierarchically
porous carbon materials can simultaneously realize high
capacity and long-cycling durability. The specific capacitance
has been recorded to be up to 753.0 F g
� 1
at 0.5 A g
� 1
with
capacity retention as high as 96.7 % even after 5,000 cycles.
Also, the assembled symmetric cell provided a high energy
density of 17.36 Wh kg
� 1
at 250 W kg
� 1
. The effects of yellow
and green colors and different activation temperatures on the
properties of electrode materials were systematically studied.
The results showed an excellent electrochemical performance
in biomass carbon electrode materials, which would facilitate
the development of a high-quality energy system and a green
supercapacitor.
Introduction
With the worsening of the environment and depletion of
resources, the human society is in crisis. Therefore, there is a
critical need to develop high energy conversion efficiency
storage devices. Supercapacitors (SCs) have attracted attention
because of the merits of large power density, good cycling
stability, fast charging, and discharging.
[1]
Thus, the super-
capacitor is being used in various ways for electronics as well
as electric vehicles with hybrid drive and pulse technology.
[2]
However, the SCs have low energy density, which limits the
range of the original application. Generally, it is proportional to
the supercapacitor’s energy density with capacitance and
voltage window.
[3]
The potential window can be increased by
assembling an asymmetric supercapacitor. Although high
capacitance electrode materials have been widely used in the
positive electrode of the asymmetric supercapacitor, it is
difficult to obtain negative electrodes that have high capaci-
tance. Generally, carbon materials with large negative potential
windows are used as negative electrode.
[4]
Carbon materials,
such as, graphene, carbon nanotubes, porous carbon, etc. are
versatile. They are not only non-toxic, chemically stable, and
readily conduct electricity, but also have peculiar properties
can accelerate electrolyte ions diffusion.
[5]
However, the low
capacitance of traditional carbon materials reduces the energy
density of SCs. Finding a negative electrode with high
capacitance remains a challenge, which limits the development
of SCs. Specifically, increasing the specific surface areas (SSA)
can improve the capacitance and rate performance by adjust-
ing the pore distribution of carbon.
[6]
The wettability can be
increased by doping heteroatoms on the carbon surface, and
the electrolyte-accessible areas can be enlarged.
[7]
However,
these electrode materials are usually prepared using expensive
and unsustainable raw materials.
[8]
Given all these require-
ments, biomass is seen as a high-efficiency carbon precursor
because of its economical and continuable potential. Using
special processes, well-distributed pore size and physicochem-
ical stability were exhibited in some biomass-derived carbons.
[9]
They have the advantages of large potential windows, stable
physicochemical properties, easy synthesis, and are often used
as a positive pole in asymmetric SCs.
[10]
Additionally, biochar
raw materials tend to contain a mass of oxygen-containing
functional groups, such as C � O, C = O, and carboxyl groups,
improving their performance over traditional carbon
materials.
[11]
For example, Wu et al. used albizia flowers to
prepare hierarchical porous carbon microrods for SCs. The
specific capacitance (Cs) reached 406 F g
� 1
at a current density
of 0.5 A g
� 1
in a 6 M KOH electrolyte.
[12]
It could improve
capacitance performance and energy storage in SCs by
selecting suitable biomass precursors and catalysts. Regarding
SCs, biomass is a promising electrode material. However, there
are still many factors preventing its further use: finiteness of
geographical distribution, production, and transportation.
[13]
Celery, which is widely planted in China, naturally has several
elements that can be doped, and people always eat celery
stalks but discard celery leaves as garbage. Celery stem had
been used to prepare porous carbon in supercapacitors with
good charge storage capacity, but unfortunately it was
prepared by expensive freeze-drying and the SSA was only
507.73 m

.
[14]

are wasted, and celery leaves and celery stems have different

Therefore, a quick absent template method was developed
to efficiently synthesize porous carbon by carbonizing celery
leaves and activating them with KOH (Scheme 1). In this view,
the effects of activator and carbonization temperature on the
formation of biomass carbon pores were investigated. Also, the
impact of yellow leaves and green leaves on the electro-
chemical performance of SCs was investigated in detail.
Results and Discussion
Materials characterization. Scanning electron microscopy
(SEM) was used to study the morphology of celery-derived
porous carbon. The SEM images of five samples were
compared. Figure 1a-b show random distribution of some
pores on the surface of the carbon material that green leaves
with 800 ° C activation temperature (aGCL-800). Several pores
were derived from the development of gases, such as H
2
and
CO
2
in the carbon layers during the fission of KOH. Figure 1c-d
show the magnified SEM images of porous carbonized at
different conditions. When carbonized green leaves at 700 ° C,
aGCL-700 (Figure 1c) has only some nanopoles due to low
carbonization temperature and graphitization. Due to the lack
of activator action, many pores were not formed in the GCL-
800 that green leaves with 800 ° C activation temperature
absence with activator (Figure 1d). Combined with BJH desorp-
tion, the average pore diameter of aGCL-800 and aGCL-900
(Figure S1a) aYCL-800 (Figure S1b) carbonized yellow leaves
with 800 ° C activation temperature is 3.942, 3.941 and
3.938 nm, respectively. The Transmission Electron Microscope
(TEM) images (Figure S1c) indicate the presence of micropores
that were randomly distributed and irregularly shaped. The
TEM images (Figure S1d) also explain the deficiency of any
graphitic domains, revealing the non-crystalline property of
aGCL-800.
[15]
Therefore, suitable temperature and activator
action promote aGCL-800 to have a large number of pore size
structure at the same time, which successfully improves the
SSA of the electrode material and is conducive to the electro-
lyte and electrode material adequately contact.
The powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectra, X-ray
photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and the Brunauer-Emmett-
Teller (BET) were used to show the chemical structure of the
GCL-800, aGCL-800, and aYCL-800. In Figure S2, XRD was used
to investigate the crystal structure of the graphitized porous
carbon material. All XRD patterns demonstrate two character-
istic peaks at 2θ of 22 ° (002) and 43 ° (100). There was a broad
diffraction peak of carbon in XRD patterns which confirmed the
amorphous carbon structure.
[16]
The Raman spectra of GCL-800, aGCL-800, and aYCL-800

Symmetric Supercapacitor Device. The geometric structure
of bipolar supercapacitor is considered to be the best indicator
of the material performance of electrodes. Carbon materials
with excellent potential windows can be directly assembled
into symmetric supercapacitor (SSC) without the need for
complex asymmetric devices. Two aGCL-800 electrodes were
made into two-electrode cell and the electrochemical charac-
terization was tested. As expected, the stable operating voltage
can be extended up to 1.0 V (Figure S10). Figure 4a shows the
CV curves of the symmetrical two electrode with different scan
rates. It showed a rectangular shape, with tiny faradaic peak
and showed the behavior of double-layer capacitive and
pseudocapacitive.

supercapacitor: surface control and diffusion control.

The remarkable electrochemical performance of aGCL-800
for SCs could be ascribed to the following aspects: 1) celery leaf
itself also showed excellent capability since it is rich in fiber
and elements. These advantages guaranteed the fabrication of
pores and improvement of surface wetting ability; 2) due to the
activation of KOH, pores of all sizes were distributed in original
starting material so that the ions could continue to flow rapidly
resulting in a high Cs; 3) More importantly, aGCL-800 has some
factors of heteroatom doped, high graphitization degree and
hierarchical porous structure so that it showed excellent
electrochemical performance. Many doped heteroatoms (N, O,
S) could be considered profitable for enhancing capacitance
through increased ion adsorption sites and offer extra faradaic
pseudo-capacitance. Improvements to the graphitization re-
sulted in further improvement in the electrical chemical proper-
ties of the active material and increasing the conductivity of
the material. When large-scale ions proceed discharge/charge,
several macropores played an important part in buffering
them, meanwhile the main function of the micropores was to
increase the capacitance of the double layer. With the large

Conclusion
Here, a simple strategy was developed using pyrolysis and KOH
activation to activate porous carbon SCs. The different heter-
oatoms in the material, carbonization temperature, and
introduction of activator played a great role in the improve-
ment of subsequent electrochemical performance. As previ-
ously mentioned, the aGCL-800 showed many excellent
features: the structure of hierarchical porous, large SSA, higher
degree of graphitization, and Cs. Moreover, the SSC showed
that the Cs reached 125 F g
� 1
at 0.5 A g
� 1
and the Cs showed
minimal change after 10000 cycles, demonstrating an excellent
cycling stability. The supercapacitance performances of aGCL-
800 were much better than most studies reporting carbon-
based material from biomass. This study offers a useful way to
produce finely hierarchical porous carbonaceous substances via
a simply chemical activation-assisted pyrolysis process. It could
turn biomass into modern energy storage equipment and
could be used in other energy storage materials and equip-
ment.
Experimental Section
All the reagents and solvents were purchased from chemical
suppliers and used without any further purification.
Synthesis of the celery leaves-derived porous carbon: The waste
celery leaves that were collected from the canteen of Harbin
Normal University washed multiple times with deionized water to
remove visible mud. The cleaned green celery leaves were placed
in a cool, ventilated place and dried naturally. Then the dried celery
leaves were put into a tube furnace and calcined at a temperature
of 600 ° C for 1 h under the protection of nitrogen. The carbonated
samples were mixed with KOH at the mass ratio of 1 : 4 in an
aqueous solution. The dried celery leaves/KOH mixture was then
heated at 800 ° C under a nitrogen atmosphere. The product was
washed with 1 M HCl and distilled water thoroughly for several
times until the pH = 7 and then it was dried at 80 ° C and named it
aGCL-800 which the figure is activation temperature. For compar-
ison, the different activation temperature (700 ° C, 900 ° C) were also
investigated in the above process. The samples were denoted as
aGCL-700 and aGCL-900. What’ s more, in order to study the effect
of activator on the properties of the prepared samples, the GCL-
800 absence with activator was also investigated in above process.
The yellow celery leaves which procedure was similar with aGCL-
800 were named as aYCL-800.
Preparation of the working electrode: The working electrode was
prepared by pressing a homogeneous paste of 80 % (wt.) active
material, 10 % (wt.) carbon black and 10 % (wt.) polyvinylidene
fluoride (PVDF) onto carbon paper followed by overnight drying at
60 ° C. The mixture was brushed evenly onto the carbon paper with
a pipettor. And the area of each electrode piece was 1 cm × 1 cm =
1 cm
2
. The thickness of the working electrode is about 60 μm.
Before used, the electrodes were vacuum dried at 80 ° C for 12 h
thus the mass loading of the active material of electrode was about
2.00 mg cm
� 2
. The mass of positive and negative active material
aGCL-800 are 2.040 mg and 2.872 mg, respectively. So, the total
mass of active material for device case is 4.912 mg when assembled
device.
